title: Sar Buland Khan Submits Under Pressure

blocks.text: Once the position is lost, Sar Buland Khan abandons the hope of recovering it by force and turns to negotiation. Charat Singh's advance and seizure of the surrounding advantage make clear that resistance now risks humiliation without any realistic path to victory.

Envoys pass between the camps while the Sikhs tighten their hold, confiscate wealth, and treat the captive commander as a figure whose status itself can be monetized. In that atmosphere, a huge ransom was demanded, turning the khan's surrender into a public measure of Sikh leverage.
The page thus joins military success to political theatre. Captivity, tribute, and the visible reduction of a major Mughal figure all deepen Charat Singh's authority.
